text:
noah: Thanks for the AH recap. Two quick clarifying Qs on runway/actions: 1) if a team wants to prepay for a spot capacity vendor to get a 15% discount, who approves? 2) Is there any immediate hiring pause or new thresholds?

ethan (Eng): We're evaluating a vendor that asks for a 3mo prepay. Numbers look good but cash hit is front-loaded. Want to understand the approvals and how this affects runway math.

maria (CFO): Short answers: prepay > $10k -> Procurement + Finance Ops intake; prepay <= $10k may be handled via expedited review but P-card not for prepay. Hiring: no company-wide freeze today but we will tighten role approvals if runway metrics worsen.

noah: Is the $10k threshold total spend or monthly?

maria (CFO): Total spend for the commitment. Example: 3mo @ $4k/mo = $12k -> triggers standard intake.

dylan (Finance Ops): For anyone submitting, use FIN-300 and include: cash impact by month, expected unit-cost savings, cancellation windows, and counterparty risk. We'll model runway impact in the form. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/FIN-300

zoe (People Ops): On hiring, what are the new guardrails for IC vs hire backfills? any expedited path for customer-critical roles?

maria (CFO): We will maintain critical hiring (revenue-facing, security, ops) but require Hiring Committee sign-off for roles above L5 or >$200k OTE. Backfills for mission-critical roles still allowed with manager + People Ops approval.

sam (CEO): Quick add: our priority is velocity and runway balance. If a prepay materially reduces unit cost and has clear payback within 9-12 months, we will be supportive — but finance needs visibility before cash is committed.

ethan (Eng): If Finance Ops signs off on the ROI but Procurement flags legal issues, does that stall approval?

dylan (Finance Ops): We triage in parallel. Procurement/legal flags will be surfaced in the intake; we aim for a 3-5 business day turnaround for standard intakes if counterparty diligence is needed. Expedite for high ROI cases.

noah: Are there any temporary changes to P-card limits?

maria (CFO): P-card policy unchanged: general limit $5k per transaction, manager approval required. For rapid infra bursts under $5k, P-card is fine. Anything that touches customer data or requires vendor onboarding must go through vendor-onboarding even if under $5k.

ethan (Eng): What about committed Dedicated capacity? earlier AH mentioned exec sign-off thresholds. Could you repeat?

maria (CFO): Exec sign-off required for committed contracts >= $50k annualized. That is $50k run-rate, not total contract value. If unsure, include estimated annualized figure in FIN-300.

noah: One more: if a team agrees to a multi-month commit that reduces unit costs but we later need to scale down, what's the typical rollback clause?

maria (CFO): Standard approach: negotiate a 30-day scale notice and try to include partial-termination or credit windows. Procurement will prioritize flexibility for infra contracts. Flag variability in the intake so we can negotiate those terms up front.

procure-bot: Created FIN-300-11: "3mo prepay inquiry - infra cost reduction" assigned to dylan.

sam (CEO): Thanks everyone. TL;DR: do the FIN-300 for prepay/commitments, include cash flow + ROI, involve Procurement early, People Ops for headcount, and Finance will fast-track high-ROI asks.

noah: Thanks 74. I'll loop the infra team and submit FIN-300 with the two scenarios (conservative/aggressive).

dylan (Finance Ops): One small tip for submitters: include a simple two-row table in the form with assumptions  conservative vs optimistic utilization so we can plug numbers quickly.

maria (CFO): We'll publish the updated thresholds and a short decision tree in the docs page by EOD.

noah: Great, appreciate it.
